verifications.claim: The Selective Service System will automatically register eligible men (citizens and residents aged 18–25) for the military draft starting in December 2026 using existing federal data.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Eligible men will automatically be registered... by December"; "most males between 18 and 25"; "Beginning on December 18, 2026... male U.S. citizens and other U.S. residents... on the basis of other federal government databases"; "integration with federal data sources."
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm automatic registration by SSS for men 18-25 (citizens/residents) using federal data sources starting December 2026.

verifications.claim: The automatic registration change is part of the fiscal 2026 National Defense Authorization Act.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "mandated in December 2025 as part of the fiscal 2026 National Defense Authorization Act"; "Congress approved automatic registration... as part of the 2026 National Defense Authorization Act"; "provision of the Fiscal Year 2026 National Defense Authorization Act."
verifications.reasoning: All sources explicitly state it is part of the FY2026 NDAA.

verifications.claim: The automatic registration change removes the need for individual self-registration.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "streamline the previous process of self-registration"; "Men will no longer be required to register themselves"; "will register men automatically rather than require them to register themselves."
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly state shift from self-registration to automatic by SSS.

verifications.claim: The responsibility for registration shifts from individuals to the Selective Service System.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "transfers responsibility for registration from individual men to SSS"; "transfers responsibility for registration from individual men to SSS through integration with federal data sources."

verifications.claim: The Selective Service System will pull data from other federal agencies.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "integration with federal data sources"; "on the basis of other federal government databases"; "pulling data from existing databases."
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm use of other federal data sources/databases, implying agencies.

verifications.claim: Almost all male U.S. citizens between 18 and 25 years old are affected.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Most men between the ages of 18 and 25"; "All male U.S. citizens... between the ages of 18 and 25"; "most males between 18 and 25."
verifications.reasoning: Sources state most/all eligible male citizens 18-25 must/are registered.

verifications.claim: Male immigrants residing in the U.S. between 18 and 25 years old are affected.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "immigrants who don’t register may lose their U.S. citizenship"; "immigrant non-citizens who are between the ages of 18 and 25"; "certain categories of non-U.S. citizen men... permanent residents, refugees, asylum seekers, and undocumented immigrants."

verifications.claim: The automatic registration is not a reinstatement of the draft.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "The U.S. has not had a draft since... 1973"; "Automatic registration does NOT mean a draft"; "in case a military draft is authorized."
verifications.reasoning: All sources clarify registration ≠ draft reinstatement; draft inactive.

verifications.claim: Reinstatement of the draft requires congressional and presidential authorization.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Congress would need to pass legislation to amend the Military Selective Service Act to authorize the president"; "if authorized by the President and Congress."

verifications.claim: Registration is still mandatory by law.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "required to register with the Selective Service"; "required by law to have registered"; "register men automatically rather than require them to register themselves."
verifications.reasoning: Law mandates registration; now automatic by SSS.

verifications.claim: Failure to be registered (even if automatic registration fails) can result in the loss of federal student loans.
verifications.label: AMBIGUOUS
verifications.evidence: "can prevent people from receiving state-funded financial aid"; "denied student loans"; but "federal law requiring Selective Service registration as a condition of federal financial aid... overridden in December 2020."
verifications.reasoning: News mention student loans (ambiguous federal/state); Wikipedia contradicts for federal aid post-2020; no mention of auto failure.

verifications.claim: Failure to be registered (even if automatic registration fails) can result in the loss of jobs.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: "ineligibility for many federal employment opportunities"; "denied... government jobs (including federal, state and local)".
verifications.reasoning: Current penalties for non-registration include job loss; vague on post-auto or if auto fails.

verifications.claim: Failure to be registered (even if automatic registration fails) can result in the loss of citizenship opportunities.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "immigrants who don’t register may lose their U.S. citizenship"; "eligibility for citizenship, if they are immigrants."
verifications.reasoning: Explicit for immigrants; applies to non-registration generally, though auto failure unaddressed.

verifications.claim: The potential military draft database has seen declining registration rates
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "registration rates … declined in recent years, dropping from 84%... to 81%"; "Registration rates for the draft have declined in recent years but remain high... 81%... from 84%."
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated with specific declining percentages.
